The passage describes existentialism as a philosophy that empowers individuals to forge their own paths, but it mentions that this perspective can be challenging for some. The word "daunting" refers to something that may seem overwhelming or intimidating, particularly in the face of the complex and uncertain choices one must make.

a): It means giving support or confidence, which is the opposite of daunting. The passage does not suggest that existentialism is encouraging for everyone.

b): It means frightening or causing fear or anxiety. This fits the context well because the passage mentions that the perspective can be challenging or overwhelming to some.

The subject of the Passive Voice is changed into the object of the Active Voice. Also, the object of the Passive Voice is changed into the subject of the Active Voice.

The removal of the "to be" verb [being] and the preposition 'by' is necessary while changing the voice of the sentence from Passive to Active.

The Passive voice in this question is in Past Continuous. Thus, the Active voice will also be in Past Continuous.

In Passive voice, the format is: Object of the Active voice (Subjective case) + was/were + being + V3 + by + Subject of the Active voice (Objective case).

Thus, the format of Active voice is: Subject + was/were + V1 + ing + Object.

For example:

Math was being practised by Amit. (Passive Voice)

Amit was practising Math. (Active Voice)

Given the context that she had a flight to catch, packed her bags, and booked a cab, the final action should imply an unexpected interruption or delay - such as falling asleep.

Option d) looked out means to be watchful or look outside, which doesn't suit the intended contrast.

Hence, option (c) is the answer.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: d) She was taking notes while listening attentively to the lecture.

In this sentence, both "was taking" and "listening" use the -ing form to express actions that were in progress at a particular moment. "Was taking" is part of the past continuous tense, showing continuity. "Listening" also conveys an action occurring simultaneously and continuously with note-taking.

In option a), "rising" is a participial adjective describing "tides," not an ongoing action.

In option b), "running" is a gerund functioning as the object of "love."

In option c), "shimmering" is a participial adjective describing "stars."

Only option d) clearly uses the "-ing" form to express the continuity of actions or events.

Note: Gerund: Gerund is a verb form that functions as a noun, ending in -ing. A gerund can be either the subject or object of a sentence in English. Example: "Everybody enjoyed her dancing and singing at the party." The words 'dancing' and 'singing' are gerunds.

Participle: A word formed from a verb (e.g. going, gone, being, been) and used as an adjective (e.g. working woman, burnt toast) or a noun (e.g. good breeding). In English, participles are also used to make compound verb forms (e.g. is going, has been). Consider the sentences given below:

Dancing at the party, the women fell on the ground.

Encouraged by her parents, Rita went on to pursue her passion.

The highlighted word in the first sentence is of the form Verb + ing and is used as a present participle. It is used to denote an action that is going on or incomplete or imperfect.

The highlighted word in the second sentence is of the form verb + ed. It is used as a past participle. It denotes the completed action or state of the thing spoken of.

A past participle ends with the following: -ed, -d, -t, -en, or -n.

One should take great care and never get confused between a gerund and a present participle. They use the same forms but perform different functions: a gerund is a verbal noun, while a present participle is a verbal adjective.

The Simon Commission, officially known as the Indian Statutory Commission, was appointed by the British government in 1927 to assess the progress of constitutional reforms in India as mandated by the Government of India Act 1919. The purpose was to review the effectiveness and impact of the reforms introduced in the Act. However, the Commission faced significant controversy and opposition in India for several reasons.

Lack of Indian Representation

The Simon Commission consisted entirely of British members and did not include any Indian representatives. This omission was deeply resented by the Indian political leaders and the public, as it was seen as an affront to Indian aspirations for self-governance and a denial of their right to be involved in the decision-making process regarding their own future.

Popular Protest

The arrival of the Simon Commission in India led to widespread protests and demonstrations across the country. People from all walks of life, led by prominent leaders of the Indian National Congress and other political parties, actively protested against the Commission's composition.

Impact on Indian Nationalism

The Simon Commission and the protests against it played a significant role in galvanizing the Indian independence movement. It united various sections of Indian society against British colonial rule and intensified the demand for full self-government and independence.

The two most important chips on the motherboard are known as the northbridge and the southbridge. These two chips have most of the important communications and control functions provided by the motherboard.

The northbridge, also known as the memory controller hub, is connected directly to the processor via the front-side bus to system memory via the memory bus, and to the southbridge via an internal bus.

The southbridge also known as the I/O controller hub connects to the processor indirectly via the northbridge and controls slower devices such as the hard drive, USB, audio, video, LAN, PCI, I/O controller, and integrated device hardware, such as, sound card, video card, USB, PCI, Ethernet, IDE, ISA, Bios. If there is one chip, then everything is controlled by that chip. The PCI bus connects the southbridge to the northbridge.
